thread:
mara: ok pushing this here — proposal to merge the `console_metrics` and `route_metrics` namespaces into a single `metrics_v2` envelope to simplify quota routing and reduce duplicate attribution. outline + risks below.

jon: interested. quick tl;dr of benefits?

mara: 1) one canonical metric for route/tenant -> fewer joins in dashboard queries. 2) unified quota keys simplify the router policy (no more route vs console divergence). 3) cheaper storage overall because we can de-duplicate prefix fields and use compacted column set.

kevin: sounds promising but worried about backfill blowup. what's the plan for existing time-series and historical dashboards?

mara: plan: dual-write for 4 weeks + shadow reads for dashboards. incremental backfill in epoched batches: 7d windows, parallelism limited to avoid saturating the ingest pipeline. backfill job will emit progress to `#eng-platform` and to the runbook svc.

sasha: any schema changes to the routing key? router currently keys off `{tenant_id, route_id, route_variant}`. are we collapsing route_variant?

mara: keeping `route_variant` for now. change is to move `namespace` from top-level field into `envelope.meta.namespace` and add a `canonical_route_key` derived field. router will read `canonical_route_key` (string) to decide quota bucket. this avoids changing router code mid-rollout — we can add a compatibility adapter.

jon: compatibility adapter = proxy transform in intake? or in the ingestion service?

mara: ingestion-side adapter. config flag `ingest.enable_namespace_merge` that can be toggled per-cluster. adapter will synthesize `canonical_route_key` when missing.

dalia: from console UX side — dashboards expect `route_label` dimension. will that map cleanly?

mara: yes, we will add `route_label` as a materialized view column for queries. console team will be given a short-lived feature flag to toggle to the materialized column for selects. fallback to old join is still available during canary.

kevin: backfill safety: what about double counting during dual-write? we might end up with duplicates if both old and new paths write overlapping envelopes.

mara: good point. we'll include a dedupe step: an idempotency token `envelope.id_v2` derived from (tenant, route, timestamp, sample_hash). ingestion will dedupe on `id_v2` for 48h window. backfill job will mark reprocessed windows and exclude already-processed ids.

sasha: what about query latency — the new materialized columns change indexing. any index build plan?

mara: index plan: build new indexes concurrently on a shadow table, then swap. we're also going to add a small TTL to hot rows in the old table to keep size bounded during transition. estimated extra disk: +12% during peak.

jon: monitoring checklist?

mara: dashboards to add before enabling: 
- ingest.kv.ingest_lag_p50/p95 
- ingest.kv.duplicate_rate (per-tenant)
- console.query.p99 for the dashboard queries (before & after)
- storage.delta_bytes_per_hour (projected vs actual)
- quota_router.rejection_rate and fallback_count
- backfill.job_failure_rate and throughput

kevin: can we gate rollout on those metrics with auto-rollback?

mara: yes — pipeline will emit health events to `infra-bot`. infra-bot will auto-hold the rollout if `duplicate_rate > 0.5%` or `dashboard.p99 worsens by >20%` or `backfill.job_failure_rate > 1%` for 15m. manual override allowed by eng leads.

dalia: any user-visible changes? we need to notify CS if quota buckets change for enterprise customers.

mara: we'll produce a migration mapping table per tenant and run a dry-run audit for top 50 customers. CS will get a summary and scheduled maintenance window if we detect changes >1% of quota assignments.

jon: PR and runbook links?

mara: PR: https://git.redwood/eng-platform/pull/8123 (contains migration SQL and adapter code).
Runbook draft: https://docs.redwood/runbooks/ingest-namespace-merge (WIP).

kevin: could you paste the core migration SQL snippet? want to sanity-check.

mara: sure:
```sql
-- create v2 envelope table (shadow)
CREATE TABLE metrics_v2_shadow (
  id_v2 text PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id text,
  canonical_route_key text,
  route_label text,
  ts timestamptz,
  payload jsonb
);

-- backfill window example
INSERT INTO metrics_v2_shadow (id_v2, tenant_id, canonical_route_key, route_label, ts, payload)
SELECT
  md5(concat(tenant_id, route_id, to_char(ts, 'YYYYMMDDHH'), sample_hash)) as id_v2,
  tenant_id,
  concat(tenant_id, ':', coalesce(route_id,'-')) as canonical_route_key,
  route_label,
  ts,
  payload
FROM console_metrics
WHERE ts >= $window_start AND ts < $window_end;
```

sasha: thanks. two quick asks: 1) can we add a dry-run mode that writes to a shadow namespace and emits row counts only? 2) include query cost estimates for the backfill job so infra can budget slot usage.

mara: yes to both. backfill job has `--dry-run` and `--cost-estimate` flags. will share numbers in the runbook PR.

jon: timeline?

mara: tentative: week 0: merge adapter + shadow table create. week 1-2: dual-write + dry-run backfills on small tenants. week 3: full backfill ramp (throttled). week 4: enable read path switch for console queries. week 5: monitor, then cutover and drop old tables after 30 days of stable metrics.

kevin: I'm going to review the SQL and the index plan. can we add a smoke test that runs a sample query and compares results between old and new paths?

mara: yep — will add a `compare_outputs` smoke test in the CI that runs nightly during rollout.

infra-bot: scheduled maintenance ticket created: #MT-2248. Backfill job scheduled to start 3832180000.

dalia: thanks team. I'll sync with CS on the audit and prepare the customer comms draft.

jon: LGTM overall. please @me on the PR when ready and i'll do a quick perf review.

kevin: adding a note to the incident runbook about how to rollback the adapter quickly if router errors spike.

mara: thanks all — will iterate on runbook and PR. closing thread for now, will post updates in the PR and `eng-platform` channel.
